summary:
Konya is a province of Turkey and stands under Turkey's national legal and security framework; the danger a trans visitor faces in Konya is set by that framework rather than by any local instrument. No Konya-specific statute, incident, arrest or court ruling appears in the sources consulted for this entry, so the findings below apply country-wide and are not evidence of Konya-specific enforcement.

Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 that a leaked omnibus draft, the 11th Judicial Package, would amend the penal code to criminalise conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality with up to three years' imprisonment, and to imprison participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies for up to four years.

The same draft would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care, including surgery, from 18 to 25, and would require proof of permanent infertility plus repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals. Healthcare professionals performing such interventions would face fines and up to seven years in prison, and trans people receiving care deemed illegal would face up to three years.

Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association opposed the draft. Human Rights Watch warned that the measure would force treatment underground and expose people to arrest and pretrial detention.

Kaos GL's 2025 monitoring review found that hostility toward LGBTI+ people had become explicit state policy, recording roughly 313 violations in the year, about two and a half times the previous year's total, alongside 299 detention decisions.

The same review recorded six right-to-life violations, three of them hate-motivated killings, with transgender people the most affected group, and 89 torture or ill-treatment violations, up from 51 the prior year. Violations of freedom of expression rose from 216 to 540 over the same period.
tangentialFactors:
Kaos GL's 2025 review places the country-wide figures in a wider pattern of institutional hostility: public institutions received "Year of the Family" instructions, an LGBTI+ association was closed with criminal cases opened against 11 of its members, and artistic events were cancelled or banned. Freedom-of-expression violations rose from 216 to 540 in a single year.

Turkey's counts are high by regional comparison: 299 detention decisions were recorded in 2025 through formal and informal channels, and the total violation count rose roughly 2.5-fold year on year, indicating escalation rather than a settled baseline.
localsOnly:
For residents, the practical exposure sits in the draft package's care provisions. Gender-affirming care would be restricted to people aged 25 and over, conditioned on permanent infertility and repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals, with healthcare professionals liable to fines and up to seven years' prison and trans patients receiving care deemed illegal liable to up to three years.

Residents also bear the enforcement statistics: Kaos GL recorded 299 detention decisions and 89 torture or ill-treatment violations in 2025, up from 51 the previous year, alongside six right-to-life violations of which three were classified as hate-motivated killings, with transgender people the most affected.

Organised LGBTI+ life is constrained directly. An association was closed and criminal cases were opened against 11 of its members, and artistic events were cancelled or banned during the year.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted since the Human Rights Watch report of 29 October 2025 is unresolved in the sources consulted; the draft was unpassed at the time of reporting.

No Konya-specific enforcement data, arrest records, local police practice or provincial court decisions are documented here, and the sources do not state whether the Kaos GL national counts include incidents in Konya.

Whether the draft's criminalisation provisions would be applied by Konya prosecutors, and how local authorities in Konya treat gender-nonconforming visitors at identity checks, are not sourced and remain unresolved.
